subject: programming
title: Integer division
prompt: In Java, what is the value of the expression 7 / 2 when both operands are int?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Integer division discards the fractional part, truncating toward zero.

subject: programming
title: Remainder
prompt: In Java, what is 17 % 5?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: 17 = 3×5 + 2, so the remainder is 2.

subject: programming
title: Operator precedence
prompt: In Java, what is 2 + 3 * 4?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition: 2 + 12 = 14.

subject: programming
title: Short-circuit evaluation
prompt: Assume x is 0. Does Java evaluate 10 / x in the expression x != 0 && 10 / x > 1?

options.text: No; Java always skips the right operand of &&
No; && stops after the false left operand

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Logical AND evaluates its right operand only when its left operand is true.

subject: programming
title: A loop boundary
prompt:
How many times does this Java loop execute its body?
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { /* body */ }
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The body runs for i = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

subject: programming
title: Breaking a loop
prompt: What does break do when used directly inside a Java for loop, without a label?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: An unlabeled break exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch; here it exits the for loop.

subject: programming
title: Array indexes
prompt: For a Java array with length 6, what is the largest valid index?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Array indexes run from 0 through length − 1.

subject: programming
title: New array contents
prompt: What value is initially stored in each element of new int[3] in Java?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Java initializes primitive integer array elements to zero.

subject: programming
title: Aliasing an array
prompt: After int[] a = {1, 2}; int[] b = a; b[0] = 9; what is a[0]?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Both variables refer to the same array object; modifying it through b is visible through a.

subject: programming
title: Comparing string contents
prompt: For two non-null Java strings a and b, which expression tests whether their contents are equal?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: String.equals compares contents. == compares object references.

subject: programming
title: String immutability
prompt: After String s = "cat"; s.toUpperCase(); what is the value of s?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Strings are immutable. toUpperCase returns a new value, and that return value was not assigned.

subject: programming
title: Concatenation order
prompt: What does System.out.print("x" + 1 + 2); print in Java?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: + is evaluated left to right. After "x" + 1 produces a string, the next + concatenates 2.

subject: programming
title: Primitive arguments
prompt: If a Java method receives an int parameter and reassigns that parameter, what happens to the caller’s int variable?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Java passes argument values by value. Reassigning the local parameter does not reassign the caller’s variable.

subject: programming
title: Method overloading
prompt: Which pair of methods can be overloaded in the same Java class?

options.text: int f(int x) and double f(int x)
public f(int x) and private f(int x)

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Overloading requires different parameter lists; return type, parameter names and access modifiers alone do not distinguish signatures.

subject: programming
title: A recursion base case
prompt: Why does a recursive method usually need a reachable base case?

options.text: To force Java to use iteration
To make every call execute in constant time

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A reachable base case supplies a result without another recursive call, allowing the recursion to terminate.

subject: programming
title: Recursive factorial
prompt: Let f(0) = 1 and f(n) = n * f(n−1) for positive integers n. What is f(4)?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam

subject: programming
title: Binary search prerequisite
prompt: Which condition is required by standard binary search on an array?

options.text: The array is sorted according to the comparison used
The array length is a power of two

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The ordering lets binary search discard the half that cannot contain the target.

subject: programming
title: Linear search worst case
prompt: In the worst case, how many equality checks does ordinary linear search need to determine that a value is absent from an array of n elements?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Every array element must be checked when the target is absent.

subject: programming
title: Insertion sort on sorted input
prompt: For standard insertion sort on an already sorted array of n elements, what is the running time?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Each new element needs only a constant-time comparison to discover it is already in place.

subject: programming
title: Stack removal order
prompt: Push A, then B, then C onto an initially empty stack. Which item does the next pop return?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A stack follows last in, first out.

subject: programming
title: Queue removal order
prompt: Enqueue A, then B, then C into an initially empty FIFO queue. Which item does the next dequeue return?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A FIFO queue removes the earliest enqueued item.

subject: programming
title: A set insertion
prompt: An initially empty mathematical set receives the values 2, 2, 3. How many distinct elements does it contain?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Sets retain distinct values only: {2, 3}.

subject: programming
title: Instance fields
prompt: In Java, how is a non-static instance field normally stored across two different objects of the same class?

options.text: Only the first object has the field
Each object has its own field value
Both objects must share one value

source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Instance fields belong to individual objects; static fields belong to the class.

subject: programming
title: Dynamic dispatch
prompt: In Java, a variable of type Animal refers to a Dog object. Dog overrides the non-static method speak(). Which implementation runs for animal.speak()?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Overridden instance methods are dynamically dispatched according to the runtime object type.

subject: programming
title: Constructor purpose
prompt: What is a Java constructor primarily used for?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: A constructor runs during object creation to initialize the new instance.

subject: programming
title: Null dereference
prompt: Assume String s = null. What happens when s.length() is evaluated?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: An instance method cannot be invoked through a null reference.

subject: programming
title: Bounds checking
prompt: For int[] a = new int[3], what happens when a[3] is read?
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The only valid indexes are 0, 1 and 2; Java checks bounds at runtime.

subject: programming
title: Nested loops
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: For each of n outer iterations there are n inner iterations.

subject: programming
title: A doubling loop
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: The values before the body are 1, 2, …, 2^(k−1); after k doublings i equals n.

subject: programming
title: A recursive call count
prompt: A recursive function makes two calls on inputs of size n/2 and does Θ(n) additional work. For T(n) = 2T(n/2) + Θ(n), what is T(n)? Assume a constant-size base case.
source: VisCon authored practice · not an ETH exam
explanation: Each recursion level costs Θ(n), and there are Θ(log n) levels.
